Three national **rankings of universities in the United Kingdom** are published annually by the *Complete University Guide* and *[The Guardian](/wiki/The_Guardian "The Guardian")*, as well as a collaborative list by *[The Times](/wiki/The_Times "The Times")* and *[The Sunday Times](/wiki/The_Sunday_Times "The Sunday Times")*. Rankings have also been produced in the past by *[The Daily Telegraph](/wiki/The_Daily_Telegraph "The Daily Telegraph")* and the *[Financial Times](/wiki/Financial_Times "Financial Times")*.

British universities rank highly in [global university rankings](/wiki/College_and_university_rankings "College and university rankings") with eight featuring in the top 100 of all three major global rankings as of 2024: *[QS](/wiki/QS_World_University_Rankings "QS World University Rankings")*, *[Times Higher Education](/wiki/Times_Higher_Education_World_University_Rankings "Times Higher Education World University Rankings")*, and *[ARWU](/wiki/Academic_Ranking_of_World_Universities "Academic Ranking of World Universities")*. The national rankings differ from global rankings with a focus on the quality of [undergraduate education](/wiki/Undergraduate_education "Undergraduate education"), as opposed to [research](/wiki/Research "Research") prominence and faculty [citations](/wiki/Citation "Citation").

The primary aim of domestic rankings is to inform prospective undergraduate applicants about universities based on a range of criteria, including: entry standards, student satisfaction, staff–student ratio, expenditure per student, research quality, [degree classifications](/wiki/British_undergraduate_degree_classification "British undergraduate degree classification"), completion rates, and graduate outcomes. All of the league tables also rank universities in individual subjects.

**Mercury** is the first [planet](/wiki/Planet "Planet") from the [Sun](/wiki/Sun "Sun") and the [smallest in the Solar System](/wiki/List_of_Solar_System_objects_by_size "List of Solar System objects by size"). It is a [rocky planet](/wiki/Rocky_planet "Rocky planet") with a [trace atmosphere](/wiki/Atmosphere_of_Mercury "Atmosphere of Mercury") and a surface [gravity](/wiki/Gravity "Gravity") slightly higher than that of [Mars](/wiki/Mars "Mars"). The surface of Mercury is similar to Earth's [Moon](/wiki/Moon "Moon"), being [cratered](/wiki/Impact_crater "Impact crater"), with an expansive [rupes](/wiki/Rupes "Rupes") system generated from [thrust faults](/wiki/Thrust_fault "Thrust fault"), and bright [ray systems](/wiki/Ray_system "Ray system"), formed by [ejecta](/wiki/Ejecta "Ejecta"). Its largest crater, [Caloris Planitia](/wiki/Caloris_Planitia "Caloris Planitia"), has a diameter of 1,550 km (960 mi), which is about one-third the diameter of the planet (4,880 km or 3,030 mi). Being the most [inferior](/wiki/Inferior_planet "Inferior planet") orbiting planet, it always appears close to the Sun in [Earth](/wiki/Earth "Earth")'s sky, either as a "morning star" or an "evening star". It is the planet with the highest [delta-v](/wiki/Delta-v "Delta-v") required for travel from Earth, as well as to and from the [other planets](/wiki/List_of_planets_in_the_Solar_System "List of planets in the Solar System") in the [Solar System](/wiki/Solar_System "Solar System").

Mercury's [sidereal year](/wiki/Sidereal_year "Sidereal year") (88.0 Earth days) and [sidereal day](/wiki/Sidereal_day "Sidereal day") (58.65 Earth days) are in a 3:2 ratio, in a [spin–orbit resonance](/wiki/Tidal_locking#Planets "Tidal locking"). Consequently, one solar day (sunrise to sunrise) on Mercury lasts for around 176 Earth days: twice the planet's sidereal year. This means that one side of Mercury will remain in sunlight for one Mercurian year of 88 Earth days; while during the next orbit, that side will be in darkness all the time until the next sunrise after another 88 Earth days. P. Morgans](/wiki/J._P._Morgan "J. P. Morgan"). On September 30, the Astros clinched their fourth AL West title in the span of five seasons (which was the first time they had won four division titles in five seasons since the 1998–2001 teams); the six playoff appearances in seven seasons is the best span in franchise history. [Yuli Gurriel](/wiki/Yuli_Gurriel "Yuli Gurriel") became the second Astro to win the batting title, doing so at the age of 37 with a [batting average](/wiki/Batting_average_(baseball) "Batting average (baseball)") of .319.[[119]](#cite_note-120) The Astros beat the [Chicago White Sox](/wiki/2021_Chicago_White_Sox_season "2021 Chicago White Sox season") in the [American League Division Series](/wiki/2021_American_League_Division_Series "2021 American League Division Series") to advance to their fifth consecutive ALCS, a feat matched by only two teams in LCS history and the first since the [Atlanta Braves](/wiki/Atlanta_Braves "Atlanta Braves") of the 1990s (having made all eight contested NLCS from 1991 to 1999).
